title: Adaptive SRE-Mass Cache Sizing for Hybrid Linear Attention

contributions.purpose: Eliminates wasted memory from fixed sparse-cache sizes in hybrid linear attention by sizing the cache to actual per-step recall requirements.
contributions.mechanism: SRE-adaptive-mass caching, a training-free method that retains tokens until a target fraction p of the total Self-Recall Error (SRE) mass is captured, dynamically adjusting cache size at each update step.
contributions.evaluation: Evaluated on RULER long-context benchmarks against LoLA's fixed cache size baseline.
contributions.domain: efficient LLM inference / KV cache compression
contributions.source_quote: We propose SRE-adaptive-mass caching, a training-free method that dynamically sizes the sparse cache in hybrid linear attention based on cumulative SRE mass fraction.

contributions.purpose: Shows that adaptive cache sizing substantially reduces memory overhead with small accuracy cost.
contributions.mechanism: Measures cache size and accuracy of SRE-adaptive-mass caching on RULER Variable Tracking tasks versus a fixed-cache baseline.
contributions.evaluation: 46% cache reduction on Variable Tracking while retaining 93% of baseline accuracy (16.52% vs 17.72%).
contributions.domain: efficient LLM inference / KV cache compression
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate 46% cache reduction on Variable Tracking tasks while retaining 93% of baseline accuracy (16.52% vs. 17.72%), showing that adaptive sizing can substantially reduce memory overhead.

contributions.purpose: Validates that the SRE signal specifically, not just any importance score, is what makes adaptive cache sizing work.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation replacing SRE with attention-based importance scores (H2O-style) in the adaptive sizing procedure.
contributions.evaluation: Replacing SRE with H2O-style attention scores causes complete task failure (0% accuracy), supporting the theoretical connection between SRE and recall capability.
contributions.domain: efficient LLM inference / KV cache compression
contributions.source_quote: We show that the SRE signal is specifically critical for adaptive cache sizing—replacing it with attention-based importance scores (H2O-style) causes complete task failure (0% accuracy)...

contributions.purpose: Characterizes which task types benefit from adaptive caching versus needing larger budgets.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis of per-task behavior of adaptive caching across RULER task categories.
contributions.evaluation: Finds tasks with diffuse token dependencies (Variable Tracking) benefit most from adaptive caching, while information retrieval tasks (MQ) require higher cache budgets.
contributions.domain: efficient LLM inference / KV cache compression
contributions.source_quote: We analyze task-dependent behavior, finding that tasks with diffuse token dependencies (VT) benefit most from adaptive caching, while information retrieval tasks (MQ) require higher cache budgets.

self_declared_provenance.quote: These methods target standard softmax attention; our work addresses the distinct challenge of cache sizing in hybrid linear attention architectures where the importance signal must capture linear state approximation error rather than attention scores.

Our work builds on LoLA's sparse caching mechanism but replaces its fixed cache size with adaptive sizing based on SRE mass fraction, enabling dynamic memory allocation that responds to per-token recall requirements.

notes: Headline accuracy numbers are low in absolute terms (16.52% vs 17.72% on Variable Tracking); 'retaining 93% of baseline accuracy' refers to this ratio. Paper carries an explicit machine-generation warning with code at gitlab.com/fars-a/adaptive-sre-kv-cache-allocation.
